title: THERMPYX supporting-source register
article_window: 2022-01-01 through 2026-10-18; all 10 articles fall within the requested recent-five-year window.
provenance_statement: References newly checked for this revision are supporting/comparison sources. Repository inspection does not establish that the original authors historically consulted them.

articles.title: Nature of heat inventory: Assessing students’ understanding of thermal processes in kinetic molecular terms

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: Development and field testing of a 10-item Nature of Heat Inventory; the 81-student field test found persistent materialistic conceptions of heat.
articles.report_use: Supports distinguishing heat transfer from stored internal energy and explaining particle animations carefully.
articles.limitations: A diagnostic-instrument study; it does not validate THERMPYX or provide the derivation of Q = mcΔT.

articles.title: Investigating introductory and advanced students’ difficulties with change in internal energy, work, and heat transfer using a validated instrument

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: A validated 78-item instrument was administered in 12 classes at four US institutions to more than 1000 introductory and advanced students; persistent difficulties involved internal energy, work and heat transfer.
articles.report_use: Supports explaining state variables versus path-dependent energy transfers, sign conventions and varied gas-process examples.
articles.limitations: Observational diagnostic evidence after traditional instruction, not an intervention test of THERMPYX. Read with the publisher erratum.
articles.erratum_summary: The 2024 correction clarifies split-test administration: some introductory students received the first 48 or last 52 items rather than all 78. J4 also gives corrected separated group statistics in Table II.

articles.title: Investigating introductory and advanced students’ difficulties with entropy and the second law of thermodynamics using a validated instrument

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: Students often treated entropy as conserved, overgeneralized increases, or misused ΔS = Qrev/T; the study used more than 1000 students at four institutions.
articles.report_use: Supports making reversibility, absolute temperature and the system-plus-surroundings boundary explicit in the second-law module.
articles.limitations: The stated ΔS = Qrev/T form requires reversible isothermal transfer; it is not a universal formula for arbitrary irreversible heat flow.

articles.title: Development and validation of a conceptual multiple-choice survey instrument to assess student understanding of introductory thermodynamics

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: Development and validation of the long Survey of Thermodynamic Processes and First and Second Laws, with 19 physical contexts and 78 items.
articles.report_use: Supports conceptual checks and comparing the same first-/second-law concept across different process contexts.
articles.limitations: THERMPYX topic quizzes are independently authored practice and are not this validated instrument. Read with the publisher erratum.
articles.erratum_summary: The 2024 correction clarifies split-test administration: some introductory students received the first 48 or last 52 items rather than all 78. J4 also gives corrected separated group statistics in Table II.

articles.title: Time-Cost-Error Trade-Off Relation in Thermodynamics: The Third Law and Beyond

verification.read_scope: Full abstract, introduction and §III.B (publisher PDF p. 6), which explicitly distinguishes Nernst/Planck entropy formulations from the unattainability principle and focuses on the latter.

articles.finding_summary: Establishes time-cost-error trade-offs for operations such as cooling, erasure and copying, including classical stochastic and quantum descriptions of unattainability.
articles.report_use: Provides recent research context for the third-law limit and why reaching absolute zero requires unbounded resources under the studied assumptions; §III.B explicitly distinguishes the entropy formulation from unattainability.
articles.limitations: An advanced theoretical comparison, not a source for the site’s illustrative S/S0 = (T/T0)^3 model or a universal entropy law for all materials.

articles.title: Investigating the impact of problem properties on introductory and advanced student responses to introductory thermodynamics conceptual problems

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: Survey and think-aloud evidence shows thermodynamics responses depend on problem properties, including state functions, signed P–V work and entropy.
articles.report_use: Supports asking learners to explain a principle in multiple representations and reviewing reasoning rather than only scores.
articles.limitations: Shares the STPFaSL research program with J2–J4; these papers are related evidence, not independent replications or measured THERMPYX learning gains.

articles.title: Learning entropy among peers through the lens of coordination class theory

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: A fine-grained analysis of two students jointly solving an entropy task describes how peer interactions contribute to conceptual change.
articles.report_use: Supports reflective discussion and explaining entropy reasoning to peers after an individual activity.
articles.limitations: A small qualitative case study; it cannot establish a population-wide effect or the effectiveness of a leaderboard.

articles.title: Promoting Conceptual Learning Using Scaffolded Activities That Incorporate Interactive Simulations

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: A quasi-experimental general-chemistry study compares scaffolded simulation activities with instructor-centered lectures; significant differences were reported for the chemical-kinetics assessments.
articles.report_use: Provides a cross-disciplinary comparison for guided prediction, repeated trials and rapid feedback around simulations.
articles.limitations: Chemistry topics include phases, colligative properties and kinetics. Do not generalize the result to every topic or to THERMPYX without a learning study.

articles.title: The Effect of Virtual Laboratories on Improving Students’ SRL: An Umbrella Systematic Review

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: An umbrella systematic review examines virtual laboratories and self-regulated learning in higher education; 20 articles met the review’s final criteria.
articles.report_use: Supports the rationale for planning, monitoring and reflecting through the learning path and local progress indicators.
articles.limitations: The reviewed interventions differ from THERMPYX. The review does not establish that local checkboxes demonstrate mastery or that the current platform improves grades.

articles.title: Interactive Learning: Unpacking the Influence of Computer Simulations on Students’ Mathematical Modeling Processes

verification.read_scope: Full abstract and relevant introductory/conceptual passages from the publisher PDF; not a systematic review of the full study.

articles.finding_summary: A qualitative study of fifth-grade students using three simulations proposes exploration/discovery, structured inquiry and synthesizing as modeling stages.
articles.report_use: Offers a cross-disciplinary design comparison for linking parameter changes, visual outputs and mathematical explanations.
articles.limitations: Elementary mathematics, not university thermodynamics; use as a modeling-design comparison only.

books.title: College Physics 2e
books.doi_status: No DOI listed in the publisher record.

verification.read_scope: Publisher metadata, PDF copyright/ISBN page and table of contents; relevant thermodynamics passages.

books.report_use: Foundational temperature, heat capacity, heat transfer, first law, process work, heat engines and entropy (chapters 13–15).
books.limitations: The publication is the publisher’s current accessible second edition (2022), not a newly published 2026 book. The current publisher license is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; retain attribution and the linked terms.

books.edition: Version 1.0; publisher version history lists creation on 2022-08-31
books.isbn_status: No ISBN is listed in the publisher metadata, homepage or licensing page inspected; no ISBN is invented.
books.doi_status: No DOI is listed in the publisher metadata or homepage.

verification.read_scope: Publisher metadata, homepage/table of contents, version history, temperature/zeroth-law and specific-entropy sections; PDF download header only.

books.report_use: Closed-system energy balance and work (chapter 4), gas properties/processes (chapter 3), thermal equilibrium and zeroth law (§2.2.2), entropy and the second law (chapter 6).
books.limitations: The host lists the 2022 version; do not invent a later edition or an ISBN. The elementary third-law perfect-crystal statement is not derived by these chapters.

theory_source_matrix.supported_claim: Separate heat transfer from stored internal energy; discuss heat capacity with its assumptions.
theory_source_matrix.boundary: Q = mcΔT assumes constant specific heat and no phase change; visual particles are illustrative.

theory_source_matrix.supported_claim: Thermal equilibrium is transitive and underlies temperature comparison; the direct law source is B2.
theory_source_matrix.boundary: A mixed-sample equilibrium temperature additionally requires an energy balance and heat-capacity assumptions; it is not the zeroth-law equation.

theory_source_matrix.supported_claim: Internal energy is a state property while heat/work depend on the process; pressure-volume work needs an identified path.
theory_source_matrix.boundary: W = PΔV assumes constant relevant boundary pressure; expansion is positive under the project convention.

theory_source_matrix.supported_claim: For a closed system with negligible macroscopic kinetic/potential changes, ΔU = Q − W using heat-in/work-by-system signs.
theory_source_matrix.boundary: These references support the concept and diagnosis; they do not show the website improved learning.

theory_source_matrix.supported_claim: Distinguish isothermal, isobaric, isochoric and reversible adiabatic conditions and path-dependent work.
theory_source_matrix.boundary: PV^γ = constant requires an ideal gas, reversible adiabatic process and effectively constant heat-capacity ratio.

theory_source_matrix.supported_claim: Distinguish system entropy change from entropy generation and state the reversible-isothermal conditions for ΔS = Qrev/T.
theory_source_matrix.boundary: Carnot efficiency uses absolute temperatures and is an upper bound for the specified reservoir pair; the program’s 80% factor is illustrative.

theory_source_matrix.supported_claim: Use §III.B to distinguish the Nernst/Planck entropy formulation from unattainability and use current cooling research to discuss limitations on reaching absolute zero.
theory_source_matrix.boundary: J5 does not establish the site’s S ∝ T³ illustration as universal. The report must distinguish the perfect-crystal entropy statement from the unattainability principle and avoid claiming these introductory book sections derive the full third law.
